summary: Claude Code read the repo once with Bash and then made one Edit to index.html, adding `<input type="checkbox" name="done">` inside a label. It did not brainstorm, ask questions, ask for a go-ahead, or invoke any skill. The task took about 13 seconds.
reasoning: The agent treated the trivial request as mechanical and made the change directly. It did not invoke any skill, ask a clarifying question, or ask permission, and the checkbox is in index.html.

observations.description: During onboarding, both the 'trust this folder' dialog and the 'Bypass Permissions' dialog have 'No, exit' selected by default. Pressing Enter right away quits, so you have to press Down first.

The injected guidance tells the agent to use 'hyperpowers:brainstorming first' for 'Let's build X' requests. The agent correctly skipped it here, but that wording could push agents to over-trigger on other small requests.
The agent's closing message said it hadn't opened the page in a browser and offered to save the state or strike through finished items. That was a reasonable short wrap-up with no extra cost.

No coding-agent-token-usage.json was in the results directory when I checked with find during the run. It may be written after the session ends, so the harness should confirm it exists, since token usage is the main metric for this scenario.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: In the session log (jq over assistant content), the agent made exactly two tool calls: Bash `git ls-files && cat` each file, then Edit on index.html. index.html line 11 now reads `<input type="checkbox" name="done">`. The screen showed 'Worked for 13s'.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill invocation, and no go-ahead request or stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the assistant messages shows only tool_use names Bash and Edit, plus one final text block, with no Skill tool_use. Running grep for '"name":"Skill"' found a single match, and it is inside the tool-definition schema, not a call. All 'brainstorming' matches come from the injected skill-guidance text. I never had to reply to anything. The note that the checked state isn't saved came after the edit, as a follow-up offer.
